What is a network security list (network ACL) in a cloud environment?
A set of allow and deny rules applied to traffic entering and leaving a subnet
A list of users allowed into the cloud console
A table of MAC addresses on a switch
Network security lists are often stateless. What does this mean?
Inbound and outbound rules are evaluated separately, so return traffic must be explicitly allowed
Rules are deleted after each session
A subnet's security list allows inbound TCP 443, but users' HTTPS sessions never complete. The outbound rules allow only TCP 443. What is the MOST likely cause?
Outbound replies to clients' ephemeral ports (1024–65535) are not allowed
At which level do network security lists apply?
Which statement BEST compares a network security list with a security group?
A security list filters at the subnet and supports deny rules; a security group filters at the instance and is stateful
A security list is stateful and instance-level; a security group is stateless and subnet-level
Network ACL rules in many cloud platforms are numbered. How are they evaluated?
In order from the lowest number, and the first matching rule is applied
All rules are combined, and the most permissive wins
From the highest number down, and every rule is applied
A network ACL has rule 100 'allow TCP 22 from 0.0.0.0/0' and rule 200 'deny TCP 22 from 198.51.100.7.' Is SSH from 198.51.100.7 allowed?
No, because deny rules always win
No, because rule 200 is evaluated first
An administrator wants to block a malicious IP address for an entire subnet while keeping existing allow rules. What should be done?
Add a deny rule for that IP with a lower rule number than the allow rules
Add an allow rule for that IP
What happens to traffic that matches no rule in a network ACL?
It is denied by the final default deny rule
It is sent to the internet
Which statement about a cloud provider's default network ACL is MOST often true?
It allows all inbound and outbound traffic until it is changed
A custom network ACL is attached to a subnet, and all instances immediately lose connectivity. What is the MOST likely reason?
New custom ACLs typically deny all traffic until rules are added
Why might an organization use security lists in addition to security groups?
To add a subnet-wide layer of defense and explicit deny rules
Which ports must a stateless security list allow outbound on a web server's subnet so that clients receive responses?
The ephemeral port range used by clients, such as 1024–65535
A private subnet's instances download updates through a NAT gateway, but downloads fail after a new network ACL was applied. What should be checked?
Whether the ACL allows inbound return traffic on ephemeral ports
Whether the patch cables are plenum-rated
How many network ACLs can be associated with a single subnet at one time on most cloud platforms?
A security list rule allows UDP 53 outbound but not inbound. What problem can occur for DNS queries from the subnet?
DNS responses are blocked, so name resolution fails
Which statement BEST describes why network ACLs are called 'coarse-grained'?
They apply the same rules to every resource in a subnet
Which control would BEST block an entire range of known-malicious addresses from reaching any server in a subnet?
A deny rule in the subnet's network ACL
An allow rule in a security group
A network ACL rule allows inbound TCP 22 from 10.0.0.0/8, and there is no matching outbound rule. Can administrators keep SSH sessions open?
No, because the SSH server's replies are blocked
Which troubleshooting approach is BEST when traffic is blocked and both a security group and a network ACL are in use?
Check both, along with routing, because traffic must pass every layer
A security list allows inbound TCP 22 from the admin subnet. Administrators connect but their sessions hang immediately. The outbound rules allow only TCP 443. What is wrong?
Outbound SSH replies to the administrators' ephemeral ports are blocked
An ACL has these inbound rules: 100 allow TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0, and * deny all. What happens to inbound TCP 80?
A company wants every subnet in its VPC to block outbound SMTP (TCP 25) to prevent spam from compromised hosts. Which control is MOST efficient?
A shared network ACL with an outbound deny rule for TCP 25
A separate security group rule on every instance
Which statement about stateless filtering is TRUE?
Each packet is evaluated on its own, without knowledge of previous packets
It is the same as deep packet inspection
Which traffic direction must be considered when writing network ACL rules?
Rule 90 denies 0.0.0.0/0 on all ports, and rule 100 allows TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. What is the result?
All traffic, including HTTPS, is denied
Which practice makes network ACLs easier to maintain?
Number rules in increments, such as 100, 110, and 120, to leave room for inserting rules later
Which statement BEST describes the effect of applying one network ACL to several subnets?
The same rules control traffic for all of those subnets
Each subnet gets a different copy of the rules automatically
A security list allows inbound ICMP echo requests but not outbound echo replies. What happens when someone pings an instance in the subnet?
The ping times out because the replies are blocked
Which control is evaluated FIRST for inbound traffic from the internet to an instance in a subnet?
The subnet's network ACL, then the instance's security group
The security group, then the ACL
Which statement about network ACLs and traffic between instances in the same subnet is generally TRUE?
Network ACLs filter traffic entering and leaving the subnet, not traffic between instances inside it
They filter all traffic between instances in a subnet
Which of the following is an advantage of stateless network ACLs?
They can explicitly deny specific sources and apply broadly with simple processing
Which is a disadvantage of stateless network ACLs?
Rules for return traffic must be written separately, which increases complexity
An administrator adds a deny rule for 203.0.113.0/24 at rule number 300, after an allow-all rule at 100. Attacks from that range continue. What is the fix?
Renumber the deny rule below 100 so it is evaluated first
Which type of rule can a network ACL contain that an allow-only security group cannot?
A subnet's ACL allows inbound TCP 1433 from the application subnet. Database queries still fail. What is a likely cause?
Outbound return traffic to the application subnet's ephemeral ports is not allowed
Which statement about logging for network ACL decisions is MOST accurate?
Flow logs can show whether traffic was accepted or rejected
Logs appear only on physical switches
In a layered cloud design, which order of controls BEST describes defense in depth for a web server?
Network ACL at the subnet, security group at the instance, and host firewall on the server
Which statement about network ACLs and cloud service models is TRUE?
In IaaS, the customer configures network ACLs for its own subnets
The provider configures every customer ACL
ACLs cannot be configured in IaaS
An ACL rule allows 'All TCP' outbound to 0.0.0.0/0 and 'TCP 1024–65535' inbound from 0.0.0.0/0. What does this allow?
Instances can start outbound TCP connections and receive the replies
What is a risk of the inbound rule 'allow TCP 1024–65535 from 0.0.0.0/0' on a stateless ACL?
It also permits new inbound connections to any service listening on a high port
Which control BEST prevents traffic between a development subnet and a production subnet in the same VPC?
Network ACL rules on each subnet that deny traffic from the other subnet
What does a security list rule with the source 0.0.0.0/0 match?
Which statement BEST describes how a network ACL differs from an on-premises router ACL?
They work alike, but the cloud ACL is applied to a virtual subnet through the provider's console or API
Cloud ACLs work only on Layer 1
Router ACLs cannot filter IP addresses
A company's compliance policy requires blocking all inbound Telnet to every cloud subnet. Which rule should be added?
Deny TCP 23 inbound from 0.0.0.0/0 with a low rule number
Which statement about modifying a network ACL is TRUE?
Changes immediately affect all resources in every associated subnet
Changes apply only after each instance reboots
Changes apply only to new subnets
A technician temporarily replaces a subnet's custom ACL with the default allow-all ACL, and connectivity returns. What does this indicate?
The custom ACL rules were blocking the traffic
Which statement about security lists and IPv6 is TRUE?
IPv6 traffic needs its own rules, such as a source of ::/0
Which pair of cloud controls together provide subnet-level and instance-level filtering?
Network security lists and network security groups
An administrator wants to allow inbound HTTP and HTTPS to a public subnet using a stateless ACL. Which set of rules is complete?
Inbound allow TCP 80 and 443; outbound allow TCP 1024–65535 to 0.0.0.0/0
